question:
The sentence has been divided into three parts, identify the error segment in the sentence given below. Choose no error if there is no error in the sentence.

Before the meeting/began, he will have already/ left for his lunch break.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the future perfect tense **"will have already"** with the past tense "began."
 
• In English grammar, the sequence of **tenses** must be logically consistent.
 
• The **correct phrase** should be **"Before the meeting begins, he will have already left for his lunch break,"** ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Before the meeting begins,** he will have already **left for his lunch break."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "Before the meeting,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 2: "no error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 3.
 
• **Option 4: "left for his lunch break."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
